messages:
Ashok: Ran the post-patch canary for the KMS key rotation on canary-rt-2. Noticed a 5xx spike on inference endpoints and p95 latency jumped from ~90ms to ~340ms. Can we triage?
SecBot: ALERT canary-rt-2 | canary-check failed | 5xx_rate=11.8% > threshold(3%) | p95=340ms | job=runtime-canary
Molly: Saw the same from the logs — many requests seeing `invalid signature` followed by retries. Could be key version mapping mismatch. I'm going to pause new canaries. :hand:
Liam: If it's signature verification failing, likely a KV cache of public key or wrong key-id mapping in the config. Which key version did the deploy use?
Ashok: Deploy used key version v3 -> key-id mapping in secrets-manager shows v2 still referenced by runtime nodes. I pushed a mapping update during the rollout step.
Jane: Repro script (quick):
```
# smoke test against canary
curl -sS -X POST https://canary.rt.redwood.internal/v1/infer -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -w "\nstatus:%{http_code} time:%{time_total}\n"
```
Running that locally returns 500 + `invalid signature` in JSON.
Molly: I'm going to roll the canary back to pre-rotation mapping (v2) and run smoke. If that drops 5xxs we confirm mapping bug. Rolling back now.
OncallBot: Deploy rollback initiated for canary-rt-2 by Molly. Link: https://ci.redwood/inventory/rollback/5231
Liam: Also check KV-cache TTL on runtime nodes — if they cache the public key for 24h we need a cache-bust step in the rotation runbook.
SecBot: Note: CVE triage flagged rotation-runbook missing cache-bust step during earlier review (ticket SEC-2026-72).
Molly: Rollback complete. Running smoke now...
Jane: Smoke after rollback: 200s returned, p95 back to ~85ms for 100 samples. Looks good.
Ashok: Great. Root cause summary so far: rotation pipeline updated key version in secret store, but runtime config update and cache-bust were out of sync -> runtimes validated with old public key and produced sig errors and retries which increased latency.
Liam: Action items: 1) Add explicit cache-bust (synchronised refresh) to rotation playbook. 2) Add preflight check to ensure runtime key-id and secret-store key-version match. 3) Add a short-lived canary flood test (k6) to detect p95 regressions >2x baseline.
Molly: I'll file a followup PR to the runbook and patch the rotation job to update runtime-config before switching active key.
Jane: Suggested PromQL to detect this automatically: 
```
sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="runtime",route="/v1/infer",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (instance)
/ sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="runtime",route="/v1/infer"}[5m])) by (instance)
```
Alert when > 0.03 for 3m.
Ashok: Good. Also add a regression alert on p95: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 0.2` (adjust threshold per route).
Liam: For prioritization: this was a high-severity customer-facing regression so mark rotation-runbook fix as P0 for this sprint. Also run a dependency check for KMS client libs (we bumped the client recently) — although cause looks orchestration not lib bug.
SecBot: Created ticket SEC-2026-88: "KMS rotation: add cache-bust + preflight + canary flood" assigned to Molly.
Molly: I'll also add a short perf-check step to the post-patch validation checklist: run `k6` script for 60s at small QPS and assert p95 within 1.5x baseline. Example: `k6 run --vus 10 --duration 1m k6/canary_rotation.js`
Ashok: Thanks everyone. Closing the canary incident for now. We'll track SEC-2026-88 and follow up with a brief postmortem snippet in incidents channel. :white_check_mark:
Jane: Postpatch validation additions: add smoke, key-id sync check, cache-bust, k6 perf, and PromQL alerts. Will include test snippets in the runbook PR.
OncallBot: Incident closed by Ashok. Duration: 00:12:45.
Molly: TL;DR — don't flip key versions before runtime refresh; run cache-bust & perf smoke as part of rotation.
Liam: Added note: when we do private/on-prem rotations make the cache-bust step idempotent and tolerates network partitions.
Ashok: I'll draft the postmortem and link here once ready. Thanks.
